page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.8xlarge is an arm64-based compute-optimized virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs from an Ampere Altra processor running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.c6r.8xlarge delivers average multi-core and single-core performance. In stress-ng tests, it achieved a multi-core CPU score of 57,239.02 and a single-core score of 1,789.68. While single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show weaker performance profiles, multi-threaded operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a strong bzip3 multi-threaded decompression score of 217.66 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 2,274.67 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 156.84 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The system also demonstrates capable database performance, processing 44.07 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 12,731.25 on PassMark database operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64 architecture of the Ampere Altra processor offers a highly competitive performance-per-watt and resource density profile compared to traditional x86 architectures, making it a cost-effective choice for multi-threaded workloads that do not require specialized vector instructions like AVX. Given its compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2 and lack of local storage, this instance supports workloads such as containerized microservices, multi-threaded web serving, software compilation, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
